subject: Independent joint Gaussian random field fitting with the same observation precision

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: Independent joint Gaussian random field fitting with the same observation precision
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to fit a joint model of two independent Gaussian random field that is separated by a line in a box regoin.

Below is the code that I have constructed for this task:
library(geoR)
library(tidyverse)
library(INLA)
library(inlabru)

set.seed(123)
# simulate two sides
sim_data_1 <- grf(2000, cov.pars = c(1, 0.15), mean = -1, cov.model = 'matern', kappa = 2)
sim_data_2 <- grf(2000, cov.pars = c(0.5, 0.05), mean = 1, cov.model = 'matern', kappa = 2)

# line separating
a = 0.5
b = 0.25

idx1 <- a*sim_data_1$coords[,1] + b > sim_data_1$coords[,2]
idx2 <- a*sim_data_2$coords[,1] + b < sim_data_2$coords[,2]

x_coord <- c(sim_data_1$coords[idx1,1], sim_data_2$coords[idx2, 1])
y_coord <- c(sim_data_1$coords[idx1,2], sim_data_2$coords[idx2, 2])

z <- c(sim_data_1$data[idx1], sim_data_2$data[idx2]) + rnorm(sum(idx1) + sum(idx2), 0, 0.2)

sim_data <- data.frame(x = x_coord, y = y_coord, z = z)

ggplot(sim_data, aes(x,y)) + geom_point(aes(color = z))

a <- 0.5
b <- 0.25

X <- c(0,1,1,0)
Y <- c(0,0,1,1)
region <- Polygon(cbind(X,Y))
region <- SpatialPolygons(list(Polygons(list(region),'region')))
region <- SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(region, data.frame(id = region@polygons[[1]]@ID, row.names = region@polygons[[1]]@ID))
plot(region)

data <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = sim_data$x, y = sim_data$y),
  coords = c("x", "y")
)

data$z <- sim_data$z
data$idx <- ifelse(a*sim_data$x + b < sim_data$y, 1, 0)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(boundary = region,
                       max.edge = c(0.01, 0.05), cutoff = 0.01, max.n.strict = 600L)

spde1 <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2,
                          prior.range = c(1, 0.5),
                          prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.5))

spde2 <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2,
                          prior.range = c(1, 0.5),
                          prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.5))

cmp <- ~ mu1(1) + mu2(1) + f1(geometry, model = spde1) + f2(geometry, model = spde2)

form1 <- z ~ mu1 + f1
form2 <- z ~ mu2 + f2

lik1 <- like(formula = form1, family = 'gaussian', data = data[data$idx == 1,])

lik2 <- like(formula = form2, family = 'gaussian', data = data[data$idx == 0,])

#spv <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(spv, data = data.frame(id = 1:nrow(as.data.frame(spv))))

system.time(
  fit <- bru(components = cmp, lik1, lik2, options = list(bru_options(bru_options_get(),bru_verbose=TRUE),
                                             control.inla=list(int.strategy="grid")))
)

summary(fit)

But the above model returns me the scenario where the observational precision is assumed to be different for the two separate regions. How do I modify the code so that both fields have the same observation level precision parameter?

Thank you very much!
David

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Independent joint Gaussian random field fitting with the same observation precision
parts:
when you have two likelihood models you'll get one precision parameter
for each

if you want the same precision parameter, you need use just one model

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Independent joint Gaussian random field fitting with the same observation precision
parts:
This is a slightly tricky one define as a model, as you might run into
checks for whether a data point used by one of the fields is outside
the mesh of the other field. But in those cases I believe
inlabru/fmesher it will just set the value to zero. I think this might
work, by making it explicit which points are to be inked to which
field:

cmp <- (what you already had)
form <- z ~ (mu1 + f1) * (idx == 1) + (mu2 + f2) * (idx == 0)
lik <- like(formula = form, family = "gaussian", data = data)
fit <- bru(components = cmp, lik, options = ...)
